data.title: SpaceX (SPCX) Completed Its First Lock-Up. Here's What Investors Should Watch Next
data.description:
SpaceX (SPCX) completed its first major post-IPO lock-up expiration on August 6, allowing about 911.5 million shares to become eligible for trading. The unlock more than doubled the company's public float, but it did not trigger the wave of insider selling that many investors had feared. SPCX climbed 6.1% to close at $114.92 on Thursday and edged higher in Friday's trading. Investors are now turning their attention to the next round of share unlocks and whether insiders begin selling in the weeks ahead.

Claim 55% Off TipRanks

SPCX has a long & short ETF? Explore SPCM & SPCG

The First Unlock Was Only the Beginning

Thursday's unlock covered only about 20% of SpaceX's locked shares.

Before the event, only about 638.9 million shares, or roughly 4.9% of the company's outstanding shares, could be freely traded. After the unlock, the public float increased to about 1.55 billion shares, raising the freely tradable portion to roughly 11.9%.

Importantly, the event did not create new shares or dilute existing shareholders. It simply allowed employees, insiders, and early investors to sell shares that were previously restricted.

More Share Unlocks Are Coming

The next wave of unlocks could come sooner than many investors expect.

Another 455.8 million shares could become eligible for trading if SpaceX stock closes above $175.50 for at least five of the 10 trading days around the company's quarterly earnings report.

Even if that condition is not met, more scheduled unlocks are approaching. About 319 million shares are set to become eligible on August 20, another 319 million on September 9, and 59 million more on September 10.

By December 8, about 40% of SpaceX's outstanding shares could be freely tradable. The remaining 60%, including CEO Elon Musk's stake, is expected to remain locked until mid-2027.

What Investors Should Watch Next

The next question is no longer how many shares become eligible for trading. It is whether insiders actually decide to sell them.

Heavy insider selling could increase the supply of tradable shares and weigh on sentiment. On the other hand, limited selling could reassure investors that early shareholders remain confident in SpaceX's long-term outlook.

Investors will also continue watching the company's execution after its first earnings report as a public company. SpaceX recently reported 92% revenue growth but also outlined plans for heavy AI infrastructure spending. How the company delivers on those plans could remain just as important as the upcoming share unlocks.

Is SpaceX a Good Stock to Buy? 

On TipRanks, SPCX has a Moderate Buy consensus rating based on 23 Buys, six Holds, and two Sell ratings. The average SpaceX price target of $232.11 implies 101.98% upside potential from current levels.

data.title: Why Micron Stock (MU) Is Standing Out in the AI Memory Race
data.description:
Micron (MU) stock gained about 6% over the past five trading days, even as the memory sector came under pressure. On Thursday, Micron slipped just 1.3%, while Western Digital (WDC) fell about 13%, SanDisk (SNDK) dropped nearly 7%, and SK Hynix (SKHY) lost around 5%. Analysts believe Micron's stronger exposure to HBM and DRAM, along with its long-term customer agreements, is helping the stock hold up better than many of its peers.

Claim 55% Off TipRanks

Double your WDC exposure with Tradr's WDCX

Why Analysts Think Micron Is Better Positioned

Memory stocks have traditionally moved through sharp boom-and-bust cycles as new supply entered the market. However, many analysts believe AI is making this cycle different, with demand staying stronger for longer.

In a recent report, ThinkEquity analyst Ashok Kumar reiterated a Buy rating on Micron stock today and lifted his price target by 1,400% to $900 from $60. He believes demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM), data centers, and long-term supply agreements should keep Micron's earnings above normal levels through fiscal 2027. He noted that HBM requires more than three times the wafer capacity needed to produce the same amount of DDR5 memory. That makes it harder for new supply to catch up, helping support memory pricing.

Kumar added that investors are now looking beyond today's shortage and focusing on whether enough qualified supply will reach the market by 2028.

Long-Term Agreements Strengthen the Outlook

Analysts also point to Micron's growing use of multi-year customer agreements as another reason for confidence.

The company has already sold out 100% of its HBM capacity for 2026, while a significant portion of its 2027 production has also been reserved under long-term agreements. Those deals provide better visibility into future demand than memory makers typically had during previous cycles.

Micron has also signed 16 strategic customer agreements across the data center, automotive, and consumer markets. Together, those contracts cover about 20% of expected DRAM volumes and roughly one-third of NAND volumes over the contract period.

The stronger demand is already showing up in Micron's financial results. In its latest quarter, revenue surged 346% year over year to $41.46 billion, while non-GAAP gross margin expanded to 84.9% from 39% a year earlier.

Wall Street Still Sees About 78% Upside for MU Stock

Wall Street remains highly bullish on Micron. According to TipRanks, 29 analysts rate the stock a Strong Buy, with an average price target of $1,570, implying about 78% upside from the latest closing price.

Recent analyst views include:

  • Bank of America: Analyst Vivek Arya reiterated a Buy rating, saying lower-cost AI models are likely to increase, rather than reduce, memory demand.
  • Citi: Analyst Atif Malik reiterated a Buy rating with a $1,400 price target, implying about 59% upside.
  • Bernstein: Analyst Mark Li maintained a Buy rating and a $1,300 price target, suggesting about 47% upside.
  • KeyBanc: Analyst John Vinh reiterated a Buy rating and raised his price target to $1,750 from $1,600, implying nearly 99% upside. He expects tight memory supply to continue supporting pricing and earnings.

Is MU Stock a Buy, Sell, or Hold? 

Currently, Wall Street has a Strong Buy consensus rating on Micron stock based on 29 Buys and one Hold. The average MU stock price target of $1,570.00 indicates 78% upside potential.

data.title: Trade Desk Stock (TTD) Sinks as Weak Q2 Earnings Prompt Multiple Rating Downgrades
data.description:
Shares of advertising technology platform Trade Desk (TTD) plunged 28% in Friday's pre-market trading after several Wall Street analysts downgraded their ratings in reaction to weak Q2 earnings and disappointing guidance. Analysts from multiple firms, including BMO Capital, Truist, Baird, and Raymond James downgraded their ratings on TTD stock, citing macro and company-specific headwinds.

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks

Here's Why BMO and Baird Analysts Downgraded Trade Desk Stock

BMO Capital analyst Brian Pitz downgraded Trade Desk stock to Hold from Buy and lowered his price target to $15 from $38, citing "durable headwinds and additional share loss over the next 12 months." The 5-star analyst noted that the Q2 revenue and adjusted EBITDA miss was due to subdued macro conditions, brands moving to low-cost programmatic deals, and internal execution mistakes. Given the weak Q3 outlook, Pitz now expects 2026 and 2027 revenue to decline by 3% and 8%, respectively.

Likewise, Baird analyst Vikram Kesavabhotla downgraded TTD stock to Hold from Buy and slashed his price target to $9 from $27. The analyst said that Trade Desk significantly lagged the Street's expectations due to a tough macro backdrop, intense competition, and significant internal execution headwinds. Kesavabhotla noted that the shift toward digital and programmatic advertising didn't help in driving a recovery in TTD's business. Despite major leadership changes and product innovation, the analyst sees "limited visibility at this stage."

Truist and Raymond James Move to the Sidelines on TTD Stock

Truist Securities analyst Youssef Squali downgraded Trade Desk stock to Hold from Buy and cut the price target to $16 from $35. Like Pitz and Kesavabhotla, Squali also noted macro challenges and internal execution issues. He highlighted headwinds related to leading CPG (consumer packaged goods) and Food & Drink clients like Procter & Gamble (PG) due to geopolitical and tariff woes and executive turnover at the company. While Squali expects the new leadership to resolve the internal issues, he thinks that the "fix is likely to take several quarters to positively affect growth."

Meanwhile, Raymond James analyst Andrew Marok downgraded TTD stock to Sell from Hold, citing the Q2 miss and a "sharply negative" third-quarter outlook. He expects macro challenges and clients preferring lower-cost media to weigh on spending on Trade Desk's platform. Marok expects these headwinds to impact Q3 performance, with the company guiding its first-ever non-pandemic year-over-year revenue decline despite potential tailwinds from political spending.

Overall, Marok expects Trade Desk's recovery to be difficult. Given persistent revenue declines and margin pressures, the analyst finds it tough to justify Trade Desk's premium.

Is TTD Stock a Buy, Hold, or Sell?

Wall Street has a Hold consensus rating on Trade Desk stock based on 18 Holds, five Sells, and three Buys. The average TTD stock price target of $16.43 indicates 7% downside risk from current levels.

These ratings and price targets could change as more analysts react to the poor Q2 results and weak outlook.

data.title: Michael Burry Is Shorting Oracle and Nebius. Here's Why He's Bearish
data.description:
The Big Short investor Michael Burry has taken bearish positions against Oracle (ORCL) and Nebius Group (NBIS), arguing that some companies investing heavily in AI infrastructure may be overstating earnings by depreciating expensive graphics processing units (GPUs) too slowly. If Burry is correct, AI infrastructure companies could eventually face higher depreciation charges, reducing reported earnings even if revenue growth remains strong.

Claim 55% Off TipRanks

Two ETFs for long or short leverage on NBIS

Burry revealed that he shorted Oracle at an average price of $144.63, returning to a bearish position after previously covering his short. He also established a larger short position in Nebius at $211.77. Burry said he avoided NBIS put options because they were too expensive, with implied volatility exceeding 100%.

Both Oracle and Nebius have benefited from the AI boom. Oracle has secured major AI cloud contracts, while Nebius has raised its long-term revenue outlook as it expands its AI computing capacity. The new positions reinforce Burry's broader bearish view on AI infrastructure spending. He has also disclosed short positions in Nvidia (NVDA), Micron (MU), and Palantir (PLTR).

Why Is Burry Bearish?

Burry's main concern centers on GPU depreciation. AI companies spend billions on Nvidia-powered servers, but they recognize those costs over several years through depreciation. Burry argues that AI hardware is becoming obsolete much faster than companies assume because newer, more powerful chips are released every year. If GPUs need to be replaced sooner than expected, companies may have to write down those assets faster, reducing future profits.

He estimates that Oracle's earnings could be overstated by roughly 26% to 27% by 2028 if depreciation assumptions prove too optimistic.

Why Is Burry Targeting Nebius?

Nebius has rapidly expanded its AI infrastructure and recently disclosed about $27 billion in AI compute contracts with Meta (META), highlighting strong demand for GPU capacity.

However, Burry believes Nebius faces the same depreciation risks as others because its business relies heavily on costly GPU clusters that may lose value faster than expected. Year-to-date, NBIS stock has surged 126.8%.

Burry's bearish stance comes just days before Nebius is scheduled to report quarterly earnings, when investors will closely watch the company's capital spending plans and long-term outlook.

The Other Side of the Argument

Not everyone agrees with Burry's thesis. Many analysts argue that AI infrastructure remains supply-constrained, with demand from hyperscalers such as Microsoft (MSFT), Meta, and OpenAI continuing to outpace available GPU capacity. They believe strong customer demand and long-term AI contracts should help companies earn attractive returns on their investments despite rapid technological advances.

data.description:
Bernstein analyst Zhihan Ma on Thursday reaffirmed her Buy rating on wholesale retailer Costco (COST). She maintained her confidence in "the longevity of Costco's growth runway." She noted that the retailer continues to expect to launch about 300 new warehouses over the next 10 years.

Why Bernstein Remains Bullish on Costco

In the new report, Ma maintained her price target of $1,194 on Costco shares. The target suggests about 26% upside ahead. The analyst expects Costco's growth to be driven by its international expansion.

Ma contended that Costco's potential return is attractive relative to the risks of owning the stock. She gave the rating after Bernstein hosted an investor meeting with Gary Millerchip, Costco's chief financial officer. The meeting focused on areas such as warehouses, membership growth, e-commerce, and agentic AI.

Costco Eyes Growth through Warehouse Expansion

According to Ma, Costco's warehouse plans mean it intends to open about 30 new warehouses every year. This is higher than the retailer's historical average of about 20 to 25 new warehouses every year.

"This is supported by Costco being more creative with real estate (e.g., a new warehouse in LA under an affordable housing unit, a warehouse in Mexico City with a park and soccer field on top of the building)," Ma explained.

She further pointed out that Costco is opening standalone gas stations. These are being launched in select markets where the retailer already has a presence but believes it can add more capacity.

Bernstein Shares More on Costco's Warehouse Plan

According to Ma, just about half of those new warehouses are to be in the U.S., the retailer's largest market. The others will be launched in other parts of the world.

Over the next 12 months, however, two-thirds of new openings will still be in the U.S. The rest will focus on advanced markets such as the UK, Spain, Canada, and Mexico.

data.title: Sweetgreen Stock (SG) Slumps as Investors Leave Their Greens Over Food Illness Outbreak
data.description:
Shares in salad group Sweetgreen (SG) wilted 14% in premarket trading today as investors fretted about the impact of the U.S. cyclosporiasis food poisoning outbreak on its sales.

Claim 55% Off TipRanks

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks

Uncertain Pace of Recovery

Yesterday, Sweetgreen presenting its Q2 earnings report, said that it had seen reduced consumer demand for fresh prepared foods due to the multistate outbreak of cyclosporiasis since mid-July. The pace and timing of recovery remain uncertain, it said.

It now expects a 7% and 8% decline in annual same-store sales, compared with its previous forecast for a 2% to 4% drop.

The current outbreak, tied to recalled iceberg lettuce from central Mexico, has led some U.S. consumers to buy less lettuce and avoid some restaurant chains as the outbreak raises concerns about food safety. It is reportedly one of the largest outbreaks caused by foodborne illnesses in recent U.S. history.

America is in the midst of its worst year on record for a cyclosporiasis outbreak. Since May 1, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has confirmed or is investigating more than 18,000 cases of the illness in 45 states, and has reported 423 hospitalizations.

The illness, which can be contracted by consuming food — typically raw fruits and vegetables — or water contaminated with feces, can cause diarrhea, nausea and other gastrointestinal symptoms.

No Lettuce Link

Sweetgreen, however, reiterated in its results that it does not use iceberg lettuce on its menu and has had no indication from U.S. health authorities or its suppliers that it is linked to the outbreak. Despite this its shares have slumped 15% in the last three months.

data.title: ByteDance Is Building a 10T Parameter AI Model to Take On Anthropic's Mythos
data.description:
ByteDance, the parent company of TikTok, is developing a new artificial intelligence (AI) system with 10 trillion parameters that could rival Anthropic's flagship Mythos model. According to reports, the model is now in pre-training, which typically lasts three to six months before it is released.

Claim 55% Off TipRanks

High conviction NVDA bears now have this Tradr ETF

ByteDance Targets One of the World's Largest AI Models

According to reports, ByteDance's upcoming model would be more than three times larger than Chinese startup Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 model, which has 2.8 trillion parameters. It would also be close in size to Anthropic's advanced Mythos model, based on industry estimates.

Notably, parameters are used to measure how much an AI model learns during training to recognize patterns and perform tasks. While more parameters usually mean a larger model, they do not always make it more capable.

Meanwhile, industry estimates suggest Anthropic's Mythos 5 has about 8 trillion parameters, while Fable 5 has around 5 trillion. However, neither Anthropic nor ChatGPT creator OpenAI has officially disclosed the size of their latest AI models, making direct comparisons difficult.

ByteDance Accelerates China's AI Race

ByteDance is joining a growing group of Chinese AI firms to build trillion-parameter models. Before the release of Moonshot AI's Kimi K3, Chinese AI and tech companies like Meituan and DeepSeek led the country's AI sector with models containing about 1.6 trillion parameters.

However, ByteDance's latest project now adds to China's push to build larger and more advanced AI models as competition with U.S. AI labs heat up. The company has also joined hands with Chinese tech firm Unitree Robotics to move beyond AI models and build physical humanoid robots.

What Is the Best AI Stock to Buy? 

ByteDance is still a private company with no publicly traded stock yet. However, investors looking to explore AI stocks can consider top players such as Nvidia (NVDA), Meta Platforms (META), and Google (GOOGL).
